story.text:
STORY (60–90 s promo)

1. Ada registers her personal agent at Agent Registry. One tap issues an agent credential offer.
2. She pastes the link to her agent. The wallet collects the credential: Registry shows Issued.
3. "Get me two tickets for Friday." The agent opens Lantern Tickets and picks two seats.
4. To hold them, checkout asks to sign in with a wallet. A person would share their own credential; the agent shares its agent credential. No password, no CAPTCHA.
5. The agent's wallet asks Ada, its owner, to approve the sign-in. She approves.
6. Lantern creates the agent's account: Welcome, Ada's OpenClaw. The agent confirms the order.
7. Seats held. The agent tells Ada it's done.

Line to land: "Your agent proves who it is. You decide what it shares."

principles.text:
DESIGN PRINCIPLES

• One idea per screen. Each screen is a single video beat.
• State is the hero: Offer created → Issued, Sign in → Welcome → Seats held. Big, legible status, so motion can animate it.
• Flat 2D, no gradients, no 3D. Shapes, type and one accent per brand.
• The credential is a physical-feeling card: the same card appears in Registry, wallet and checkout.
• The wallet is the agent's: it holds the agent's credential and keys, and asks the owner before sharing.
• One door for everyone: Lantern doesn't ask who is buying. People and agents both sign in with a wallet credential.
• Agent-readable by design: links are real links with visible text; nothing hides behind a CAPTCHA.
• Calm trust (Registry: white, ink, trust blue) vs evening energy (Lantern: night ground, lantern amber).
• Type: Geist for UI, Geist Mono for IDs, Bricolage Grotesque for Lantern's display.
